questions.question: Reyan purchased a laptop for ₹56,000 and a scanner-cum-printer for ₹22,000. He sold the laptop for a 20% profit and the scanner-cum-printer for a 15% profit. What is his profit percentage?
questions.questionHtml: <!-- x-tinymce/html -->Reyan purchased a laptop for ₹56,000 and a scanner-cum-printer for ₹22,000. He sold the laptop for a 20% profit and the scanner-cum-printer for a 15% profit. What is his profit percentage?
questions.solution:
Given:

Cost price of laptop = ₹56,000

Cost price of scanner-cum-printer = ₹22,000

Profit on laptop = 20%

Profit on scanner-cum-printer = 15%

Formula Used:

Total Cost Price (CP) = Cost price of laptop + Cost price of scanner-cum-printer

Total Selling Price (SP) = Selling price of laptop + Selling price of scanner-cum-printer

Profit Percentage = \(\frac{Total\ Profit}{Total\ CP} \times 100\)

Calculation:

Selling price of laptop = CP of laptop + Profit on laptop

⇒ Selling price of laptop = ₹56,000 + (20% of ₹56,000)

⇒ Selling price of laptop = ₹56,000 + (0.20 × ₹56,000)

⇒ Selling price of laptop = ₹56,000 + ₹11,200

⇒ Selling price of laptop = ₹67,200

Selling price of scanner-cum-printer = CP of scanner-cum-printer + Profit on scanner-cum-printer

⇒ Selling price of scanner-cum-printer = ₹22,000 + (15% of ₹22,000)

⇒ Selling price of scanner-cum-printer = ₹22,000 + (0.15 × ₹22,000)

⇒ Selling price of scanner-cum-printer = ₹22,000 + ₹3,300

⇒ Selling price of scanner-cum-printer = ₹25,300

Total CP = ₹56,000 + ₹22,000

⇒ Total CP = ₹78,000

Total SP = ₹67,200 + ₹25,300

⇒ Total SP = ₹92,500

Total Profit = Total SP - Total CP

⇒ Total Profit = ₹92,500 - ₹78,000

⇒ Total Profit = ₹14,500

Profit Percentage = \(\frac{Total\ Profit}{Total\ CP} \times 100\)

⇒ Profit Percentage = \(\frac{14,500}{78,000} \times 100\)

⇒ Profit Percentage = \(\frac{145}{780} \times 100\)

⇒ Profit Percentage = \(18 \frac{23}{39}\)%

The correct answer is option 2.

questions.question: During the previous year, the price of an electronic item increased by 10%, and this year, the price of the same item decreased by 10%. If the price of the electronic item at present is ₹66,000, then what was the price of the discussed electronic item in the beginning of the previous year? (Rounded off to one decimal place)
questions.questionHtml: During the previous year, the price of an electronic item increased by 10%, and this year, the price of the same item decreased by 10%. If the price of the electronic item at present is ₹66,000, then what was the price of the discussed electronic item in the beginning of the previous year? (Rounded off to one decimal place)
questions.solution:
Price at the end of previous year = P + (10P/100)  = (110P/100)

This year, the price decreased by 10% from the price
at the end of the previous year,

Price at present = (110P/100)  - (10/100)(110P/100) = 0.99P

Given that the price at present is ₹66,000, 

⇒ 0.99P = 66,000 

⇒ P = 66,000 / 0.99 = 66,666.67

questions.question: A trader bought two articles for Rs.490. He sold one at a loss of 20% and the other at a profit of 16%. If the selling price of both articles is same, then the cost price (in Rs.) of the article sold at 20% loss is:
questions.questionHtml: A trader bought two articles for Rs.490. He sold one at a loss of 20% and the other at a profit of 16%. If the selling price of both articles is same, then the cost price (in Rs.) of the article sold at 20% loss is:
questions.solution:
Given:

Cost price of articles = Rs.490

Loss % = 20%

Profit % = 16%

Formula:

Loss % = (CP - SP)/CP × 100

Profit % = (SP - CP)/CP × 100

Calculation:

Let cost price of one article be Rs.a and cost price of two article be Rs.(490 - a).

Selling price of one article = a × 80/100 = Rs.4a/5

Selling price of other article = (490 - a) × 116/100 = Rs.(568.4 - 29a/25)

Then,

⇒ 4a/5 = 568.4 - 29a/25

⇒ 49a/25 = 568.4

⇒ a = 290

∴ Cost price of article which sold at loss of 20% is Rs.290.

questions.question: If 60 chairs are bought for Rs. 24,560, then how many chairs must be sold for Rs. 24,560 to earn a profit of 20 percent?
questions.questionHtml: If 60 chairs are bought for Rs. 24,560, then how many chairs must be sold for Rs. 24,560 to earn a profit of 20 percent?
questions.solution:
CP per chair = 24,560/60 = Rs. 409.33

SP per chair = Cost price per chair + (Profit/100) × Cost price per chair

= 409.33 + (20/100) × 409.33 = Rs. 491.19

Number of chairs = 24,560/491.19 = 50

questions.question: A shopkeeper buys oranges at the rate of 10 oranges for ₹50 and sells them at the rate of 12 oranges for ₹74. Find his gain or loss percentage.
questions.questionHtml: A shopkeeper buys oranges at the rate of 10 oranges for ₹50 and sells them at the rate of 12 oranges for ₹74. Find his gain or loss percentage.
questions.solution:
CP of 10 oranges = ₹50, SP of 12 oranges = ₹74

CP of 1 orange = ₹50 / 10 = ₹5, SP of 1 orange = ₹74 / 12 ≈ ₹6.1667

Gain per orange = SP - CP = ₹6.1667 - ₹5 = ₹1.1667

Gain % = (Gain / CP) × 100 = (₹1.1667 / ₹5) × 100 ≈ 231/3%.

questions.question: A tea seller used to make 50% of profit by selling tea at ₹9 per cup. When the cost of ingredients increased by 25%, he started selling tea at ₹ 10 per cup. What is his profit percentage now?
questions.questionHtml: A tea seller used to make 50% of profit by selling tea at ₹9 per cup. When the cost of ingredients increased by 25%, he started selling tea at ₹10 per cup. What is his profit percentage now?
questions.solution:
Initial cost price = 100/(100 + 50) × 9 = (100/150) × 9 = ₹ 6

Final cost price = 6 × (125/100) = ₹ 7.5

The profit percentage = (10 - 7.5)/7.5 × 100 = (2.5/7.5) × 100 = \(33\frac{1}{3}\)%

questions.question: Anil bought some articles at 6 for Rs. 8 and sold them at 10 for Rs. 12. His percentage loss or gain is:
questions.questionHtml: Anil bought some articles at 6 for Rs. 8 and sold them at 10 for Rs. 12. His percentage loss or gain is:
questions.solution:
Concept:

First, equal the number of articles sold and brought so that the cost price of the number of articles sold can be determined. Then calculate the profit or loss percentage.

Formula used:

Loss % = [(CP - SP)/CP] × 100

Calculation:

Taking LCM of the number of articles sold and brought;

We get 30.

CP of 30 articles = 8 × 5 = Rs 40

SP of 30 articles = 12 × 3 = Rs. 36

Loss % = [(40 - 36)/40] × 100

⇒ (4/40) × 100

⇒ 100/10

⇒ 10% 

∴ His percentage of loss is 10%

questions.question: A person bought two buffaloes for Rs. 11,520. One is sold at a loss of 15% and the other is sold at a gain of 19%. If the selling price of both buffaloes is equal, find the cost price of the first one.
questions.questionHtml: A person bought two buffaloes for Rs. 11,520. One is sold at a loss of 15% and the other is sold at a gain of 19%. If the selling price of both buffaloes is equal, find the cost price of the first one.
questions.solution:
Given:

Total cost price of two buffaloes = ₹11,520

One buffalo sold at a loss of 15%

Other buffalo sold at a gain of 19%

Selling price of both buffaloes is equal

Formula used:

Selling Price (SP) = Cost Price (CP) × (1 ± Loss/Gain %)

Calculation:

Let the cost price of the first buffalo be ₹x

⇒ Cost price of the second buffalo = ₹(11,520 - x)

SP of first buffalo = x × (1 - 15/100) = x × 0.85

SP of second buffalo = (11,520 - x) × (1 + 19/100) = (11,520 - x) × 1.19

Since SP of both buffaloes is equal:

⇒ x × 0.85 = (11,520 - x) × 1.19

⇒ 0.85x = 11,520 × 1.19 - 1.19x

⇒ 0.85x + 1.19x = 11,520 × 1.19

⇒ 2.04x = 13,708.8

⇒ x = 13,708.8 / 2.04

⇒ x = 6,720

∴ The correct answer is option 2.

questions.question: Ankita sold three toys. The first toy was sold for Rs. 1,500 at a profit of 25%; the second toy was sold for Rs. 2,800 at a loss of 50% and the third toy was sold for Rs. 3,500 at a profit of 25%. Find her total profit or loss percentage.
questions.questionHtml: Ankita sold three toys. The first toy was sold for Rs. 1,500 at a profit of 25%; the second toy was sold for Rs. 2,800 at a loss of 50% and the third toy was sold for Rs. 3,500 at a profit of 25%. Find her total profit or loss percentage.
questions.solution:
For the first toy:

Selling Price (SP) = 1,500, Profit % = 25

⇒ CP = 1,500 / 1.25 = Rs. 1,200

For the second toy:

Selling Price (SP) = 2,800, Loss % = 50

⇒ CP = 2,800 / 0.5 = Rs. 5,600

For the third toy:

Selling Price (SP) = 3,500, Profit % = 25

⇒ CP = 3,500 / 1.25 = Rs. 2,800 ⇒ Total Cost Price = 1,200 + 5,600 + 2,800 = Rs. 9,600

⇒ Total Selling Price = 1,500 + 2,800 + 3,500 = Rs. 7,800 ⇒ Profit or Loss =  7,800 - 9,600 = Rs. -1,800 (Loss)

⇒ Total Loss % = (-1,800 / 9,600) x 100 = -18.75%

questions.question: The price of a land passing through three hands rises on the whole by 65%. The first and second sellers earned 20% and 25% profit, respectively. Find the profit percentage earned by the third seller.
questions.questionHtml: The price of a land passing through three hands rises on the whole by 65%. The first and second sellers earned 20% and 25% profit, respectively. Find the profit percentage earned by the third seller.
questions.solution:
Let the original price of the land = Rs. 100

⇒ First SP = 100 × (1 + 20/100) = 100 × 1.2 = Rs. 120 ⇒ Second SP = 120 × (1 + 25/100) = 120 × 1.25 = Rs. 150 ⇒ Final SP = 100 × (1 + 65/100) = 100 × 1.65 = Rs. 165

Profit earned by the third seller: Initial price before third seller = Rs. 150 Selling price after third seller = Rs. 165

Third seller's profit % = ((165 - 150) / 150) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (15 / 150) × 100 = 10%

questions.question: The cost price of milk is increased to ₹62 from ₹60. The milkman sold milk at 10% profit earlier. What is his profit% now if he sells milk at the same rate?
questions.questionHtml: The cost price of milk is increased to ₹62 from ₹60. The milkman sold milk at 10% profit earlier. What is his profit% now if he sells milk at the same rate?
questions.solution:
Given:

The cost price of milk = Rs. 60 and after Rs. 62

Formula used:

Profit = Selling price - Cost price

Calculation:

Let the new profit percentage is X percent

The initial selling price on 10% profit = \(({1+{10\over100}})\ \times 60 ={110\over100}\times 60={11\times 6}= 66\)

The new profit = 66 - 62 = 4

The profit percentage = X = \({4\over62}\times 100=0.064516129\times 100=6.45\%\)

∴ The required result will  be 6.45%.

questions.question: A trader buys two articles for Rs. 3,000 each. While selling, he earns a 10 percent profit on one and loses 20 percent on the other. What will be his overall loss percentage?
questions.questionHtml: A trader buys two articles for Rs. 3,000 each. While selling, he earns a 10 percent profit on one and loses 20 percent on the other. What will be his overall loss percentage?
questions.solution:
Total cost price = 2 x Rs. 3000 = Rs. 6000

Selling price of first article = Rs. 3000 + 10% of Rs. 3000 = Rs. 3300

Selling price of second article = Rs. 3000 - 20% of Rs. 3000 = Rs. 2400

Total selling price = Rs. 3300 + Rs. 2400 = Rs. 5700

Overall loss = Total cost price - Total selling price = Rs. 6000 - Rs. 5700 = Rs. 300

Overall loss% = (Overall loss / Total cost price) x 100 = (Rs. 300 / Rs. 6000) x 100 = 5%

questions.question: A shopkeeper sold an article for Rs. 455 at a loss (in Rs.). If he sells it for Rs. 490, then he would gain an amount four times the loss, At what price (in Rs.) should he sell the article to gain 25%?
questions.questionHtml: A shopkeeper sold an article for Rs. 455 at a loss (in Rs.). If he sells it for Rs. 490, then he would gain an amount four times the loss, At what price (in Rs.) should he sell the article to gain 25%?
questions.solution:
Given:

Original selling price = Rs. 455

If he sells it for Rs. 490, then he would gain an amount four times the loss.

Desired gain = 25%

Concept used:

Loss = Cost price - Selling price

Gain = Selling price - Cost price

Selling price = Cost price × (1 + gain percentage/100)

Calculation:

let the cost price of the article be CP.

According to the question,

4 × (CP - 455) = (490 - CP)

⇒ CP = 462

Now, to make 25%, the shopkeeper has to it at  = (462 × 1.25) = Rs. 577.50

∴ At Rs. 577.50 he should sell the article to gain 25%.

questions.questionHtml: A dealer sells two machines at the rate of Rs. 15000 per machine. On one he earns a profit of 20 percent and on the other he loses 40 percent. What is his profit/loss percentage in the whole transaction?
questions.solution:
CP of 1st machine, ⇒ y × (1 + 20/100) = 15000 = Rs. 12500

CP of 2nd machine, ⇒ z × (1 – 40/100) = 15000 = 25000

Total cost price = 12500 + 25000 = Rs. 37500

Total selling price = 15000 + 15000 = Rs. 30000

Loss = 37500 – 30000 = Rs. 7500

⇒ Loss percent = loss × 100/CP = 7500 × 100/37500 = 20%

questions.question: The cost of 3 breads and 1 packet of juice at a certain store is ₹323.50. At the same store, the cost of 5 breads and 1 packet of juice is ₹433.50. What will be the cost of 2 breads and 2 packets of juice at this store?
questions.questionHtml: The cost of 3 breads and 1 packet of juice at a certain store is ₹323.50. At the same store, the cost of 5 breads and 1 packet of juice is ₹433.50. What will be the cost of 2 breads and 2 packets of juice at this store?

options.html: ₹350

questions.solution:
The cost of 5 breads + 1 packet of juice is = ₹433.50 ..............(1)

The cost of 3 breads + 1 packet of juice is = ₹323.50  ............(2)

By deducting option 2 from option 1 we get,

The cost of 2 breads is ₹(433.50 - 323.50) = ₹ 110

The cost of 1 bread is 110 / 2 = Rs 55

The cost of 5 breads Rs (55 × 5 ) = Rs 275 ........... (3)

From equation 1 and 3 we get ,

The cost of 1 packet of juice is ⇒ (433.50 -  275) = 158.50

The cost of 2 packets of juice is (158.50 × 2) = Rs 317

 The cost of 2 breads and 2 packets of juice at this store, ⇒ 317 + 110 = Rs 427

questions.question: A person sold two items selling each for ₹42,600. On the first item, he made a loss of 25%, while on the second, he gained 20%. Find his overall percentage gain or loss, giving your answer correct to one place of decimal.
questions.questionHtml: A person sold two items selling each for ₹42,600. On the first item, he made a loss of 25%, while on the second, he gained 20%. Find his overall percentage gain or loss, giving your answer correct to one place of decimal.
questions.solution:
By selling at Rs 42600 he loses by 25 % 

So cost price will be 42600 × 4/3 = Rs 56800

Again By selling at Rs 42600 he makes a profit by 20% 

So the cost price will be 42600 × 5/6 = Rs 35500

Total cost price will be 56800 + 35500 = 92300, Total sp will be 42600 × 2 = Rs 85200

Loss amount is 92300 - 85200 = 7100 , Loss percentage will be (7100/92300) × 100 = 7.69 % ≈ 7.7 %

questions.question: A shopkeeper bought 40 pieces of an article at a rate of ₹50 per item. He sold 35 pieces with 20% profit. The remaining 5 pieces were found to be damaged and he sold them with 10% loss. Find his overall profit percentage.
questions.questionHtml: A shopkeeper bought 40 pieces of an article at a rate of ₹50 per item. He sold 35 pieces with 20% profit. The remaining 5 pieces were found to be damaged and he sold them with 10% loss. Find his overall profit percentage.
questions.solution:
The total cost price = 50 × 40 = ₹2000

The profit = \(\left[\left(\frac{100+20}{100}×50 \right)×35\right]+\left[\left(\frac{100-10}{100}×50 \right)×5\right]-2000\) ⇒ (60 × 35) + (45 × 5) - 2000 ⇒ 325

The profit% = (325/2000) × 100 = 16.25%

questions.question: A trader buys 500 kg cotton for Rs. 8,000. If 10% of this cotton is spoiled due to rain, at what rate (Rs./kg) should he sell the rest to earn a 20% profit?

questions.solution:

questions.question: A customer availed a 10% discount on the purchase of a table and paid Rs. 4,950 for it. How much money would he have saved if he had bargained to get 12% discount?
questions.questionHtml: A customer availed a 10% discount on the purchase of a table and paid Rs. 4,950 for it. How much money would he have saved if he had bargained to get 12% discount?
questions.solution:
Given

Discount % = 10

Cost price = RS. 4950

Formula used

Cost Price = Market Price - Discount

Calculation

let the market price is Rs.x

so, 4950 = x - 10% of x

⇒ 4950 = 90x/100

⇒ x = (4950 × 100)/90

⇒ x = 5500

if discount rate is 12%

Then, cost price = 5500 - 12% of 5500

⇒ 5500 - 660

⇒ Rs. 4840

Money gained at 12% discount = RS.(4950 - 4840)

⇒ Rs. 110

∴ Customer would save Rs. 110, if he had bargained to get 12% discount.

questions.question: A shopkeeper bought 40 dozen eggs at Rs 1.40 each. 80 eggs were broken in transportation. He sold the remaining eggs at Rs 1.60 each. what is his profit or loss percent?
questions.questionHtml: A  shopkeeper bought 40 dozen eggs at Rs 1.40 each. 80 eggs were broken in transportation. He sold the remaining eggs at Rs 1.60 each. what is his profit or loss percent?
questions.solution:
Given:

Cost price each egg = Rs.1.40 

Selling price each egg = Rs.1.60 

Formula used:

Loss = Cost price - Selling price 

Loss percent = Loss/Cost price × 100

Calculation:

Cost price of 40 dozen eggs = 12 × 40 × 1.40 = 672 

Cost price of 80 eggs = 80 × 1.40 = 112

Cost price of 400 eggs = 400 × 1.40 = 560

Selling price of the remaining (480 - 80) eggs  = 400 × 1.60 = 640

Loss = Cost price - Selling price 

Cost price of 80 eggs that were broken in transportation will be treated as a loss. 

Loss = (560 + 112) - 640 = 32

Loss percent = 32/672 × 100 = \(4\frac{{16}}{{21}}\)% 

∴ The required loss percent is \(4\frac{{16}}{{21}}\)%

questions.question: Joseph bought two woollen jackets for Rs. 2,100 and Rs. 3,150, respectively. By selling the first at a gain of k% and the second at a loss of k%, he found that the selling price of both is the same. What is the value of k?
questions.questionHtml: Joseph bought two woollen jackets for Rs. 2,100 and Rs. 3,150, respectively. By selling the first at a gain of k% and the second at a loss of k%, he found that the selling price of both is the same. What is the value of k?
questions.solution:
Given:

Joseph bought two woolen jackets for Rs. 2,100 and Rs. 3,150, respectively.

By selling the first at a gain of k% and the second at a loss of k%.

The selling price of both is the same.

Concept used:

Selling price = Cost price (1 + profit percentage/100)

Selling price = Cost price (1 - loss percentage/100)

Calculation:

According to the question,

2100 (1 + k/100) = 3150 (1 - k/100)

⇒ (1 + k/100)/(1 - k/100) = 3/2

⇒ (100 + k)/(100 - k) = 3/2

⇒ 200 + 2k = 300 - 3k

⇒  5k = 100

⇒ k = 20

∴ The value of k is 20.

questions.question: Vijay bought a fridge and a washing machine together for Rs. 38,200. He sold the fridge at a profit of 15% and washing machine at a loss of 24% and both are sold at the same price. The cost price of the washing machine is:
questions.questionHtml: Vijay bought a fridge and a washing machine together for Rs. 38,200. He sold the fridge at a profit of 15% and washing machine at a loss of 24% and both are sold at the same price. The cost price of the washing machine is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of CP for Fridge (F) and Washing Machine (WM) based on same SP:

CPF × (100 + 15) = CPWM × (100 − 24)

CPF × 115 = CPWM × 76 ⇒ CPF : CPWM = 76 : 115

Total ratio parts = 76 + 115 = 191 units.

191 units = Rs. 38,200 ⇒ 1 unit = Rs. 200.

Cost price of Washing Machine = 115 × 200 = Rs. 23,000.

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 23,000.

Alternate Method

Given: Total CP = Rs. 38,200, Profit on Fridge = 15%, Loss on Washing Machine = 24%, SP1 = SP2.

Formulas: SP = CP × (100 + P%) ÷ 100 | SP = CP × (100 − L%) ÷ 100

⇒ Let CP of Fridge be x and CP of Washing Machine be y.

⇒ x + y = 38,200

⇒ SP of Fridge = x × 1.15 and SP of Washing Machine = y × 0.76

⇒ 1.15x = 0.76y ⇒ x = (76 ÷ 115)y

⇒ (76 ÷ 115)y + y = 38,200

⇒ (191 ÷ 115)y = 38,200

⇒ y = (38,200 × 115) ÷ 191 = 200 × 115 = 23,000

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 23,000.

Additional Information

Two same-SP articles

When two items are sold at the same price, the ratio of their Cost Prices is inversely proportional to their Selling Price percentage (100+P% or 100-L%).

Profit and Loss Calculation

Always calculate Profit or Loss on the Cost Price unless specified otherwise in the question.

questions.question: On selling a table for Rs. 210 and Rs. 420 there will be loss of L 1 % and L 2 % respectively. If L 1 - L 2 = 7, then what is the cost price of table
questions.questionHtml: On selling a table for Rs. 210 and Rs. 420 there will be loss of L<sub>1</sub>% and L<sub>2</sub> % respectively. If L<sub>1 </sub>- L<sub>2</sub> = 7, then what is the cost price of table
questions.solution:
CP = 100 × 210/(100 - L1%)  ⇒ CP = 100 × 420/(100 - L2%)

⇒ 2L1 - L2 = 100 Given, L1 - L2 = 7. 

⇒ L2 = 86%

⇒ CP = 100 × 420/(100 - 86) ⇒ CP = Rs.3000

questions.question: A man bought an article and sold it at a gain of 10%. If he had bought the article at 20% less and sold it for Rs. 1,000 more, he would have made a profit of 40%. The earlier selling price of the article (in Rs.) is:
questions.questionHtml: A man bought an article and sold it at a gain of 10%. If he had bought the article at 20% less and sold it for Rs. 1,000 more, he would have made a profit of 40%. The earlier selling price of the article (in Rs.) is:
questions.solution:
Given:

A man sold an article at a gain of 10% and if he had bought the article at 20% less and sold it for Rs. 1000 more, he would have made a profit of 40%.

Formula used:

S.P = C.P × (1 + P%/100)

P = S.P – C.P

P% = (P/C.P) × 100

Where,

S.P = Selling price 

C.P = Cost price 

P = Profit

Calculation:

Let CP be x

Then, SP = 110x/100 = 11x/10

New CP = 80% of x = 80x/100 = 4x/5

Gain = 40%

New SP = 140% of 4x/5 = (140/100) × 4x/5 = 28x/25

According to the question,

(28x/25) – (11x/10) = 1000

⇒ (56x – 55x)/50 = 1000

⇒ x/50 = 1000

⇒ x = Rs. 50,000

Hence, CP = Rs. 50,000

And SP = (11/10) × 50000 = Rs. 55000

∴ The earlier selling price of the article is Rs. 55000

questions.question: Amit sold an article for Rs. 7,000 and incurred a loss. Had he sold it for Rs. 8,750, his gain would have been three-fourth of the amount of loss that he incurred. At what price should he sell the article to get 10% profit?
questions.questionHtml: Amit sold an article for Rs. 7,000 and incurred a loss. Had he sold it for Rs. 8,750, his gain would have been three-fourth of the amount of loss that he incurred. At what price should he sell the article to get 10% profit?
questions.solution:
Given:

S.P =  Rs. 7000

Formula:

Profit = S.P – C.P

Loss = C.P – S.P

Calculation:

Let loss be x

C.P = S.P + x

⇒ C.P =7000 + x

Now, S.P = 8750 Rs

Gain = (3/4) × Loss

⇒ S.P – C.P = x × 3/4

⇒ 8750 - (7000 + x) = 3x/4 

⇒ 8750 – 7000 – x = 3x/4 

⇒ 1750 = 3x/4 + x

⇒ x = 1000 Rs   

C.P = 7000 + x = 7000 + 1000

⇒ C.P = 8000 Rs

For 10% profit

S.P = (8000 × 110)/100

⇒ S.P = 8800 Rs

∴ S.P to gain 10% profit is 8800 Rs

questions.question: A trader sells an article at 16% below its cost price. Had he sold it for Rs. 192.20 more, he would have gained 15%. The new selling price (in Rs.) of the article is:
questions.questionHtml: A trader sells an article at 16% below its cost price. Had he sold it for Rs. 192.20 more, he would have gained 15%. The new selling price (in Rs.) of the article is:
questions.solution:
Given:

A trader sells an article at 16% below its cost price. Had he sold it for Rs. 192.20 more, he would have gained 15%.

Formula Used:

Let the cost price be CP

Selling price at 16% loss = CP × (1 - 16/100)

New selling price at 15% gain = CP × (1 + 15/100)

Calculation:

Selling price at 16% loss = CP × 0.84

New selling price = CP × 0.84 + 192.20

New selling price at 15% gain = CP × 1.15

⇒ CP × 0.84 + 192.20 = CP × 1.15

⇒ CP × 1.15 - CP × 0.84 = 192.20

⇒ CP × (1.15 - 0.84) = 192.20

⇒ CP × 0.31 = 192.20

⇒ CP = 192.20 / 0.31

⇒ CP = 620

New selling price = CP × 1.15

⇒ New selling price = 620 × 1.15

⇒ New selling price = 713

∴ The correct answer is option (4).

questions.question: Some fruits are bought at 15 for Rs. 140 and an equal number of fruits at 10 for Rs. 120. If all the fruits are sold at Rs. 132 per dozen, then what is the profit percent in the entire transaction?
questions.questionHtml: Some fruits are bought at 15 for Rs. 140 and an equal number of fruits at 10 for Rs. 120. If all the fruits are sold at Rs. 132 per dozen, then what is the profit percent in the entire transaction?
questions.solution:
Let total fruits = 30.

CP of 30 fruits at 15 for Rs. 140 ⇒ (140 ÷ 15) × 30 = Rs. 280.

CP of 30 fruits at 10 for Rs. 120 ⇒ (120 ÷ 10) × 30 = Rs. 360.

Total CP of 60 fruits = 280 + 360 = Rs. 640.

SP of 12 fruits = Rs. 132 ⇒ SP of 1 fruit = Rs. 11 ⇒ SP of 60 fruits = 11 × 60 = Rs. 660.

Profit = SP − CP = 660 − 640 = Rs. 20.

Profit % = (20 ÷ 640) × 100 = 3 (1/8)%.

questions.question: On two items of equal prices, T gets 12% profit on one item and incurs 8% loss on other. What is his overall profit or loss percentage?
questions.questionHtml: On two items of equal prices, T gets 12% profit on one item and incurs 8% loss on other. What is his overall profit or loss percentage?
questions.solution:
Profit on the first item = 12% of C = 0.12C; Loss on the second item = 8% of C = 0.08C

Total Profit or Loss = 0.12C - 0.08C = 0.04C

Total Cost Price = C + C = 2C

Overall Profit or Loss Percentage = (0.04C)/(2C) × 100

Overall Profit or Loss Percentage = 0.02 × 100 = 2%

questions.question: The profit triples if the selling price is doubled. The profit percentage is:
questions.questionHtml: The profit triples if the selling price is doubled. The profit percentage is:
questions.solution:
Given:

The profit triples if the selling price is doubled.

Concept used:

Profit% = [(SP - CP)/CP] × 100

Calculations:

According to the question,

⇒ P = SP – CP ........(1)

It is given in the problem that on doubling the selling price, the profit triples, we have,

⇒ 3P = 2SP – CP ........(2)

Subtract (1) from (2), we get –

⇒ 3P - P = SP

⇒ SP = 2P .........(A)

Putting this in (1), we get,

⇒ P = 2P – CP

⇒ CP = P ........(B)

From (A) and (B), we get that SP = 2CP

[(2CP−CP)/CP]×100 

⇒ CP/CP × 100  = 100%

∴ The profit percentage is 100%.

questions.question: A buys an article for Rs.900 and sells it to B at a profit of 25%. B sells it to C, who sells it for Rs.1,350, at a loss of 10%. What profit percent (to the nearest integer) did B make?
questions.questionHtml: A buys an article for Rs.900 and sells it to B at a profit of 25%. B sells it to C, who sells it for Rs.1,350, at a loss of 10%. What profit percent (to the nearest integer) did B make?
questions.solution:
Given:

A buys an article for Rs.900 and sells it to B at a profit of 25%. B sells it to C, who sells it for Rs.1,350, at a loss of 10%.

Formula used:

SP = [(100 + profit%) / 100] × CP =  [(100 - loss%) / 100] × CP 

Profit% = [SP - CP]/CP × 100

Calculation:

ATQ, SP for A = CP for B

Now, SP for A = 125/100 ×900 = 1125 = CP for B

ATQ,  B sells it to C, who sells it for Rs.1,350, at a loss of 10%

⇒  SP for B × 90/100 = 1350 

⇒  SP for B = 1350 × 100/90

⇒  SP for B = 1500

∴ Profit% for B = (1500 - 1125)/1125 = 33.33% ≈ 33%

questions.question: The cost price of two dozen bananas is Rs. 30. After selling 15 bananas at the rate of Rs. 12 per dozen, the shopkeeper sells the remaining bananas at the rate of Rs. 5 per dozen. What is the loss percentage?
questions.questionHtml: The cost price of two dozen bananas is Rs. 30. After selling 15 bananas at the rate of Rs. 12 per dozen, the shopkeeper sells the remaining bananas at the rate of Rs. 5 per dozen. What is the loss percentage?
questions.solution:
(S.P)1 = \(\frac{15}{12}\) × 12 = 15 Rs.

(S.P)2 = \(\frac{9}{12}\) × 5 = 3.75 Rs.

Total S.P = 15 + 3.75 = 18.75 Rs.

Loss = \(\frac{30-18.75}{30}\times 100\) = 37.5 %

questions.question: A fruit seller buys 480 bananas for Rs. 1,200. Some of these bananas are rotten and hence, they are thrown away. He sells the remaining bananas at Rs. 3.5 each and makes a profit of Rs. 396. What is the percentage of bananas thrown away?
questions.questionHtml: A fruit seller buys 480 bananas for Rs. 1,200. Some of these bananas are rotten and hence, they are thrown away. He sells the remaining bananas at Rs. 3.5 each and makes a profit of Rs. 396. What is the percentage of bananas thrown away?
questions.solution:

= 24 / 480 × 100 = 5%

questions.question: The price of an article is raised by 45% and then two successive discounts of 15% each are allowed. Ultimately the price of the article is ______.
questions.questionHtml: The price of an article is raised by 45% and then two successive discounts of 15% each are allowed. Ultimately the price of the article is ______.
questions.solution:
Let CP be 100

MP = 100 + (45 × 100/100) ⇒ 145

Net Discount = 15 + 15 - (15 × 15/100) ⇒ 27.75%

Final Price = 145 - (145 × 27.75%) ⇒ 104.7625

% change = \(\frac{104.7625-100}{100}\) × 100 = 4.7625 %

The price of the article is increased by 4.7625 %.

questions.question: Two-third of a certain number of items are sold at 35% profit, 25% of items are sold at 30% loss and the remaining at 5% loss. What is the overall profit or loss percentage?
questions.questionHtml: Two-third of a certain number of items are sold at 35% profit, 25% of items are sold at 30% loss and the remaining at 5% loss. What is the overall profit or loss percentage?
questions.solution:
Given :

Two-third of a certain number of items are sold at 35% profit, 25% of items are sold at 30% loss and the remaining at 5% loss

Formula used :

Profit = cost price + profit on the cost price 

Calculations :

Let the total number of articles be 60 

Let the cost price of each article be 100 rupees 

Total cost price = 60 × 100 = 6000 rupees 

Now 

Two-third of article = (2/3) of 60 = 40 

25% of articles = 15 

Remaining article = 5 

Selling price of 40 articles = 135 rupees per article (Sold at a profit of 35%)

Total selling price of 40 articles = 40 × 135 = 5400 rupees 

Selling price of 15 articles = 70 rupees per article (sold at 30% loss)

Total selling price of 15 articles = 15 × 70 = 1050 rupees 

Selling price of remaining 5 articles = 95 rupees per article (sold at 5% loss)

Total selling price of all articles = 5 × 95 = 475 rupees 

Total selling price of all articles = 5400 + 1050 + 475 = 6925 rupees 

Profit percent = (6925 - 6000)/(6000) × 100 

⇒ \(15 \frac{5}{12}\%\)% 

∴ Profit percent will be \(15 \frac{5}{12}\%\)
